claims.claim: Herod the Great died in 4 BC (most scholars); Jesus born c. 6–4 BC.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVII.6.4, 8.1; E. P. Sanders, The Historical Figure of Jesus (1993).

claims.claim: Dionysius Exiguus fixed the AD era in 525.
claims.source: Standard; Dionysius, Liber de Paschate (525).

claims.claim: Pompey took Jerusalem in 63 BC; Herod ruled 37–4 BC; Judea a province from AD 6; Pilate governor AD 26–36.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XIV.4, XVII–XVIII; standard histories.

claims.claim: Quirinius's census of Judea dated by Josephus to AD 6; Luke 2:2 problem; no evidence of an empire-wide census under Augustus.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVIII.1.1; Raymond Brown, The Birth of the Messiah, appendix VII.

claims.claim: Josephus counts about 6,000 Pharisees; describes Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes, the 'fourth philosophy' of Judas the Galilean.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVII.2.4; XVIII.1.2–6; Jewish War II.8.2–14.

claims.claim: Josephus describes John the Baptist and his death under Herod Antipas.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVIII.5.2.

claims.claim: Papias records that Mark wrote down Peter's preaching.
claims.source: Eusebius, Church History III.39.15.

claims.claim: One early Greek manuscript (Codex Bezae) and some Old Latin read 'being angry' at Mark 1:41.
claims.source: NA28 apparatus; Bruce Metzger, Textual Commentary on Mark 1:41.

claims.claim: Kepler suggested the Jupiter–Saturn conjunction of 7 BC as the star.
claims.source: Kepler, De Stella Nova (1606), ch. 22.

claims.claim: Raymond Brown's list of points shared by Matthew's and Luke's birth stories.
claims.source: R. E. Brown, The Birth of the Messiah (1977/1993), pp. 34–37.

claims.claim: Mark calls Jesus a tekton and names brothers James, Joses, Judah, Simon (Mark 6:3); Jerome, Epiphanius and the Protevangelium on the brothers; Luther and Calvin held Mary's perpetual virginity.
claims.source: Mark 6:3; Jerome, Against Helvidius (c. 383); Epiphanius, Panarion 78; Protevangelium of James 9.

claims.claim: Sepphoris rebuilt by Herod Antipas, about four miles from Nazareth.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVIII.2.1; excavation reports.

claims.claim: 'Son of Man' appears over eighty times in the Gospels, nearly always on Jesus's lips.
claims.source: Concordance count (about 82 in the four Gospels).

claims.claim: Parables of Enoch (1 Enoch 37–71) date c. 50 BC–AD 70 by most scholars; survive only in Ethiopic.
claims.source: Nickelsburg and VanderKam, 1 Enoch 2 (2012); Charles (1917) introduction.

claims.claim: Mishnah forbids capital trials at night (Sanhedrin 4:1) and limits blasphemy to pronouncing the Name (Sanhedrin 7:5).
claims.source: Mishnah, Sanhedrin 4:1; 7:5.

claims.claim: Jeremias on Abba; Barr's reply.
claims.source: J. Jeremias, The Prayers of Jesus (1967); J. Barr, JTS 39 (1988) 28–47.

claims.claim: Hurtado, Bauckham, Ehrman, Bousset positions on early Christology.
claims.source: Hurtado, Lord Jesus Christ (2003); Bauckham, Jesus and the God of Israel (2008); Ehrman, How Jesus Became God (2014); Bousset, Kyrios Christos (1913).

claims.claim: Herod built a temple to Augustus at Paneas; Philip rebuilt it as Caesarea Philippi.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XV.10.3; XVIII.2.1.

claims.claim: Psalms of Solomon written after Pompey's capture of Jerusalem (63 BC).
claims.source: Ryle and James (1891), introduction.

claims.claim: Claimants after Herod's death: Judas son of Hezekiah, Simon, Athronges; Theudas; the Egyptian.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities XVII.10.5–7; XX.5.1; XX.8.6; Acts 5:36; 21:38.

claims.claim: Akiva hailed Bar Kosiba as 'son of the star'; rabbinic pun 'Bar Koziba'.
claims.source: Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit 4:5 (68d); Lamentations Rabbah 2:4.

claims.claim: The Targum of Isaiah 52:13 names the servant 'my servant the Messiah' and turns the suffering to his enemies.
claims.source: Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 52:13–53:12.

claims.claim: Wrede, The Messianic Secret (1901); Dahl, 'The Crucified Messiah' (1960).
claims.source: As cited.

claims.claim: Followers first called Christianoi in Antioch; Tacitus calls Christianity 'a most mischievous superstition'.
claims.source: Acts 11:26; Tacitus, Annals XV.44, tr. Church and Brodribb.

claims.claim: Josephus describes the exorcist Eleazar before Vespasian.
claims.source: Josephus, Antiquities VIII.2.5.

claims.claim: Talmud Sanhedrin 43a: Yeshu hanged on the eve of Passover, for sorcery and leading Israel astray (passage removed in censored editions).
claims.source: Babylonian Talmud, Sanhedrin 43a; Peter Schäfer, Jesus in the Talmud (2007), ch. 7.

claims.claim: Honi the circle-drawer; Hanina ben Dosa's prayer; Hanina healed Gamaliel's son.
claims.source: Mishnah Taanit 3:8; Mishnah Berakhot 5:5; Babylonian Talmud Berakhot 34b.

claims.claim: Celsus said Jesus learned magic in Egypt.
claims.source: Origen, Against Celsus I.28, I.38.

claims.claim: Hierocles compared Apollonius favourably with Jesus; Eusebius replied.
claims.source: Eusebius, Against Hierocles; Lactantius, Divine Institutes V.2–3.

claims.claim: Philostratus (c. 170–247) wrote the Life at Julia Domna's request.
claims.source: Philostratus, Life of Apollonius I.3.

claims.claim: Meier concludes the healing and exorcism tradition goes back to Jesus.
claims.source: J. P. Meier, A Marginal Jew, vol. 2 (1994).

claims.claim: Lourdes: seventy recognised cures by 2018 (the seventieth, Sr Bernadette Moriau, February 2018).
claims.source: Sanctuary of Lourdes / Diocese of Beauvais announcement, 11 February 2018.

claims.claim: Warfield argued miracles ceased with the apostles.
claims.source: B. B. Warfield, Counterfeit Miracles (1918).

claims.claim: Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) c. 125 BC; 11QMelchizedek and 4Q521 on Isaiah 61.
claims.source: Vermes, The Complete Dead Sea Scrolls in English (1997); Collins, The Scepter and the Star (2010).

claims.claim: First-century synagogues at Magdala and Gamla.
claims.source: Excavation reports (Magdala 2009; Gamla 1976).

claims.claim: Maimonides on the Messiah and on Christianity and Islam preparing the world.
claims.source: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Kings 11–12 (uncensored 11:4).

claims.claim: Nachmanides at Barcelona, 1263, before James I of Aragon: the prophets promised peace.
claims.source: Nachmanides, Vikuach (Disputation).

claims.claim: Rashi read Isaiah 53 as Israel among the nations.
claims.source: Rashi on Isaiah 52:13–53:12.

claims.claim: Justin argues for two comings.
claims.source: Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 14, 49 (c. 155–160).

claims.claim: Augustine: the New hidden in the Old, the Old made plain in the New.
claims.source: Augustine, Questions on the Heptateuch II.73.

claims.claim: Jefferson's cut-and-paste Bible (c. 1820), printed by Congress 1904; 'diamonds in a dunghill'.
claims.source: Jefferson to John Adams, 12 October 1813; Smithsonian, The Jefferson Bible (2011 ed.).

claims.claim: Paine wrote Part I in Paris and was arrested soon after (December 1793).
claims.source: Conway's introduction to The Age of Reason (1896).

claims.claim: Strauss was 27 in 1835, lost his post at Tübingen; George Eliot translated (1846).
claims.source: Schweitzer, Quest, ch. 7; Eliot's translation title page.

claims.claim: Tolstoy, The Gospel in Brief (written 1881, published 1883); excommunicated 1901.
claims.source: Standard biographies; Holy Synod decree, February 1901.

claims.claim: Lewis's trilemma in Mere Christianity Book 2 ch. 3; earlier form in John Duncan.
claims.source: Lewis (1952); Duncan, Colloquia Peripatetica (1870).

claims.claim: Hick edited The Myth of God Incarnate (1977); Schweitzer's apocalyptic Jesus (1906).
claims.source: As cited.

claims.claim: Sherwin-White: two generations too short for legend to wipe out the historical core.
claims.source: A. N. Sherwin-White, Roman Society and Roman Law in the New Testament (1963), pp. 186–193.

claims.claim: Tyrrell's 'liberal Protestant face at the bottom of a deep well'.
claims.source: G. Tyrrell, Christianity at the Cross-Roads (1909), p. 44.

claims.claim: Philippians written c. AD 55–62; vv. 6–11 often taken as a pre-Pauline hymn; Isaiah 45:23 applied to Jesus.
claims.source: Lohmeyer, Kyrios Jesus (1928); Bauckham, Jesus and the God of Israel (2008).

claims.claim: The Qur'an calls Jesus al-Masih eleven times.
claims.source: Concordance of the Qur'an; Khalidi, The Muslim Jesus (2001).

claims.claim: Buber found in Jesus his 'great brother'.
claims.source: Martin Buber, Two Types of Faith (1950), foreword.

claims.claim: Klausner, Jesus of Nazareth (Hebrew 1922).
claims.source: As cited.

claims.claim: Nicaea 325, Constantinople 381, Ephesus 431 (Theotokos), Chalcedon 451; Oriental Orthodox rejection of Chalcedon; Immaculate Conception 1854.
claims.source: Conciliar texts; Pius IX, Ineffabilis Deus.

claims.claim: Rhineland massacres 1096; expulsions from England 1290 and Spain 1492; Nostra Aetate 1965 §4.
claims.source: Standard histories; Nostra Aetate 4.

claims.claim: Duccio's Calling panel (1308–11) is from the Maestà of Siena Cathedral.
claims.source: NGA object record.
